what_happened.line: The Public Access Cable Committee voted unanimously to invest its enterprise fund in staggered Treasury bonds, with proceeds rolled into six-month bonds, on a financial adviser's recommendation.
The committee agreed to reinvest the interest rather than pay it out, and to review the fund's investments each June.
The manager reported the payroll videographer line is nearly spent with weeks left in the year, so a line item transfer is needed.
An ARPA request in three parts (studio, videographer kits, town hall audio) was presented to the select board; an expected Comcast deposit had not appeared in the ledger.
The manager and a committee member will attend a water board meeting about microphones, and a policy draft will go to the town lawyer.

why_it_matters: The cable committee's enterprise fund is public-access money kept outside the general budget, and this vote sets how it is invested and how its interest is used.

The ARPA request and the late Comcast deposit bear on how much the public-access studio and meeting broadcasts can rely on outside funding, and a select board decision on the ARPA request would affect that.
watch_next: The next PACC agenda should carry an update on the fund investments; the committee plans a review at each June meeting.
The select board's response to the three-part ARPA request, and the town lawyer's reply on the policy draft.
